oracle_fixture_boundaries: ItemStack and InventoryPlayer are deterministic count/slot fixtures.
ItemComparison delegates to an injected match predicate; ore branch returns false.
ParticipantInfo, progress storage and completion marking are in-memory fixtures.
limitations: Item/NBT/ore matching is injected; fixture predicates are not Minecraft registry evidence.
No actual game inventory writes, persistence, party lifecycle, UI or packet integration.
groupDetect, OR, auto-consume and multi-requirement consumption are rejected.
Positive requirements and nonnegative saved counters are required; overflow rejects the plan instead of reproducing legacy Java wraparound.

LegacyRetrievalStackMatcherCheck.test_environment: actual vanilla 1.21.1 classes + FTB 2101.1.36 matcher, no world/server startup

oracle_boundaries: Old NBT names delegate to actual 1.21.1 NBT classes; no 1.7.10 Minecraft runtime.
Logger and requiredItems count are fixtures; methods execute pinned source unchanged.
Source equivalence covers recognized nonnegative progress payloads only.
limitations: Unknown versions/fields/types, invalid UUIDs and negative counters retain raw NBT but cannot activate.
Raw NBT-tree preservation does not imply identical compressed bytes.
No FTB save bridge, task registry, events, party lifecycle, packet/UI integration or world/server startup.
Only AND, nonrepeat, nonsimultaneous, nonglobal, nonignored retrieval tasks; unsupported declarations block the whole plan.
Gate values, player/quest/cache classes and AND property logic are deterministic fixtures, not runtime authorization evidence.
The original task loop and database ordering run; Minecraft inventories, NBT/item predicates and task storage are fixture adapters.
K must be immutable or a deep snapshot owned by the caller; predicates must be pure.
No persistence, durable transaction, FTB callback, actual inventory write, quest completion or reward is implemented.

oracle_boundaries: BQ source executes against fixture player/quest/task objects, without 1.7.10 game runtime.
Source comparison covers slot policy, initial notification, START phase and deduplication for eligible inventory tasks.
Server isolation and post-drain scheduling are queue-contract checks, not claims about every BQ reentrant callback.
limitations: Actual vanilla menus prove absence of guaranteed initial slot callbacks; patched callback dispatch is shape-checked only here.
NeoForge event-bus registration, fake-player integration, team lookup, disconnect/respawn lifecycle and game timing are not run.
Real Sponge transformation is covered by the separate isolated transformation report, not this test.

LegacyTypedNbtJsonReaderCheck.unsupported_tag_zero: Original reader uses ID 0 for fallback inference; no lossless EndTag decoding is claimed.
LegacyTypedNbtJsonReaderCheck.negative_zero_gap: Actual 1.21.1 FloatTag/DoubleTag public factories and loaders normalize negative zero. Such inputs retain original bytes and are rejected; no reflection or global access adaptation is used.
oracle_boundaries: Original BQ decoder methods execute unchanged with old NBT names backed by real 1.21.1 NBT; the old game runtime is not launched.
Logger and NBT-name adapters are fixtures. Source comparisons cover accepted, explicitly typed values, excluding lossy coercions and modern negative-zero limitations.
The two supplied files are task definitions, never player saves; all rejection and numeric-boundary fixtures are synthetic.
limitations: Accepted means only this typed JSON decoding succeeded, not that a save is safe to activate.
Original UTF-8 bytes and JSON member-order ledger are retained separately; CompoundTag itself does not promise object-key iteration order.
Missing/zero/noncanonical tag suffixes, inferred arrays, malformed or ambiguous input, integer coercions, float overflow/underflow and negative zero are retained but not accepted.
Gson 2.10.1 non-lenient mode needs an additional lexical gate for raw string control characters, invalid escapes and uppercase literals; UTF-8 BOM inputs are conservatively retained but rejected.
Input limits: 16 MiB, depth 128, 1,000,000 nodes, numeric tokens at most 128 characters; limits reject without discarding original bytes.
No quest identity routing, envelope integration, FTB registry/save/event integration, world startup or on-disk player save modification.

oracle_boundaries: Six fixed routing methods execute unchanged; old NBT method names delegate to real 1.21.1 NBT.
The inner retrieval codec is reused, not an independent inner-persistence oracle in this test.
Canonical factory equality, definition registry, logger and touched-state bookkeeping are fixtures.
Strict rejection tests intentionally differ from source coercion, silent skip and placeholder fallback.
limitations: Accepted means interpreted candidate state, not a runnable game save.
Quest completion compounds are opaque except their UUID; no claimed/timestamp or reward behavior is executed.
No JSON parsing, real player-save import, file order selection, storage writes or cross-file lifecycle.
No FTB task registration, events, network, game runtime, server/world startup or export integration.
Raw NBT tree preservation does not assert identical serialized/compressed bytes.
Synthetic UUID progress, no real player save fixture or server lifecycle registration.
Archive stores exact source bytes but does not assert that arbitrary bytes were imported successfully.
No inventory, reward, party, network or FTB transaction was executed.
Process-halt recovery on this filesystem does not prove machine-power-loss durability or detect manual removal of the entire latest tail.
All immutable frames are retained; compaction and ledgers exceeding 64 MiB per frame are not supported and are never silently truncated.
Uses a real mainline quest definition but synthetic player progress, authorization and immutable symbolic item predicates.
logWood is a source-symbol fixture, not a mapped modern item tag or a verified registry membership set.
Imported and planned UUID states survive independent ledger close/reopen; no world save, real inventory, quest completion, reward, party lifecycle or FTB operation runs.
Individual fixed-source differential checks remain separate; this is a composition check, not a new original runtime oracle.
Actual vanilla Inventory objects use null Player references; no world/server or NeoForge transform chain executes.
Exact vanilla item predicates, authorization and participant membership are fixtures. Oak logs do not stand in for a verified legacy logWood mapping.
Count writes and rollback execute in memory only. No dirty flag, menu broadcast, event, task completion, reward or file write occurs.
Caller must enforce server main thread and revalidate definition, ledger, party and authorization. Capturing-thread confinement alone does not authenticate a caller.
Opaque/transient components without a lossless NBT representation are rejected with the live inventory preserved.
Third-party Inventory/ItemStack Mixin side effects and cross-file crash recovery have not been verified.
